Jake DeBrusk's name is all over the trade wire, and Vancouver is setting the terms. Markerzone reported Sunday that a deal is "gaining momentum, but Canucks firm on asking price," NHL Trade Rumors that the Canucks are refusing offers, and Daily Hive that there is interest but "there’s a catch." Vancouver Hockey Daily passed along what Rick Dhaliwal says the club is waiting for.

On the ice the goals are behind the chances. He has 5 goals on 7.45 expected goals (the quality of his chances) in 19 games, and his chance rate (1.38 expected goals per 60) is close to last season's 1.51, when he scored 23. Goals tend to follow chances like that. His last ten games have been thin, three points, even with his ice time up about two minutes a night. The Canucks' share of five-on-five expected goals is 7.3 points better with him on than off, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 55% of his shots coming off the rush, a style that needs a team winning pucks back. Evolving-Hockey had him facing 94th-percentile competition last season.
headline: Jake DeBrusk's trade market and his missing goals
